subject.title: Agent-created crons inherit session toolsAllow at create-time; patch toolsAllow:null is a silent no-op; claude-cli backend then refuses the job

question: How should OpenClaw handle `toolsAllow: null` from a restricted agent cron creator and any stale flagless default cron caps without making explicit CLI restrictions fail open?
rationale: The remaining behavior is real at source level, but the safe fix depends on maintainer intent for the runtime tool-policy boundary and stale-data repair semantics.

options.title: Reject Restricted Null Clears Explicitly
options.body: Keep creator-surface capping, but return a clear error for agent-side `toolsAllow: null` under a restricted creator and separately repair only provably stale default caps.

options.title: Allow Agent Null Clears Broadly
options.body: Let agent-side `toolsAllow: null` bypass creator capping, accepting a broader authority change that needs explicit security approval.

options.title: Keep Manual CLI Workaround
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document `openclaw cron edit --clear-tools` or job recreation as the supported operator repair path.

recommendation.title: Reject Restricted Null Clears Explicitly
recommendation.body: Keep creator-surface capping, but return a clear error for agent-side `toolsAllow: null` under a restricted creator and separately repair only provably stale default caps.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged marker-preservation work is closest to the current edit semantics and fail-closed split.
